3. Before disposing off the present controversy, brief facts pertaining to the accident are being reiterated as they are necessary for understanding of the background of the case.
It is a matter of record that the petitioner has filed the present petition against the respondents for grant of compensation.

Brief facts are that on 06.03.2010, Darshan Singh (hereinafter referred to as 'deceased') after finishing his duty at Sonepat was going towards his residence at Village Jonti on his motorcycle bearing no. HR-10E-8134 and at about 07:00 pm when Neelam Vs. Pramod Kumar Yadav & ors.

entities.text: Neelam Vs. Pramod Kumar Yadav & ors

sentences.text: he reached Main Qutub Garh Road, near Shiv Mandir, Village Punjab Khod, Delhi then his motorcycle collided with TATA Dumper bearing no. HR-46B-3036 which was parked on main Qutab Garh Road without any parking indications.
As a result, accident had occurred and deceased along with his motorcycle fell down on road and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
He was immediately moved to Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital, Mangol Puri, Delhi where the doctor declared him brought dead.

4. It is further a matter of record that the offending vehicle was parked in the middle of the road without any parking indication, which is owned by Ved Parkash (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no.2') and same was insured with IFFCO TOKIO General Insurance Company Ltd.
(hereinafter referred to as respondent no. 3).

Act taking into account the contributory negligence attributed to the deceased @ 40%. It was further held that the evidence of the parties already stands recorded in the claim petition.
Hence, no further evidence led nor required to be recorded nor any fresh issues pressed to be framed by the parties.

Neelam Vs. Pramod Kumar Yadav & ors.

Act.

Section 168 of M.V Act is reproduced as under: -

"On receipt of an application for compensation made under section 166, the Claims Tribunal shall, after giving notice of the application to the insurer and after giving the parties (including the insurer) an opportunity of being heard, hold an inquiry into the claim or, as the case may be, each of the claims and, subject to the provisions of 1[section 163] may make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and specifying the person or persons to whom compensation shall be paid and in making the award the Claims Tribunal shall specify the amount which shall be paid by the insurer or owner or driver of the vehicle involved in the accident or by all or any of them, as the case may be"
7.
I have heard Ld. counsels appearing on behalf of petitioner and respondents and carefully perused the record and gone through the order dated 20.09.2023, passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.
8. The main rival contention of the parties is about the age of deceased with respect to multiplicand and future prospects.

Ld. counsel for the petitioner argued that deceased though more than 40 years of age but have not attained the age of 41 years and hence multiplier of 15 and future prospectus at 40% of the established income should be considered while calculating the loss of dependency.

He relied upon Neelam Vs. Pramod Kumar Yadav & ors.
 the judgment passed by the Hon'ble High Court of India in case M.H. Uma Maheshwari and Others Versus United India Insurance Co. Ltd. And Another 2020 (3) T.A.C 53 (S.C.).
9.

, the court is of the opinion that the issue with regard to age of deceased as well as what should be the multiplicand and future prospects would be, has been dealt with by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court consisting five Hon'ble Judges in National Insurance Co.  India, wherein it was held as under :
(iv) In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

sentences.text: An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.

4
With respect to multiplier, it was further held in para 44 of the judgment, which is reproduced as under "44.
As far as the multiplier is concerned, the claims tribunal and the Courts shall be guided by Steps that finds place in paragraph 19 of Sarla Verma read with paragraph 42 of the said judgment.

For the sake of completeness, paragraph 42 is extracted below :-
"42.

We therefore hold that the multiplier to be used should be as mentioned in Column (4) of the table above (prepared by applying Susamma Thomas, Trilok Chandra and Charlie), which starts with an operative multiplier of 18 (for the age groups of 15 to 20 and 21 to 25 years), reduced by one unit for every five years, that is M-17 for 26 to 30 years, M- 16 for 31 to 35 years, M-15 for 36 to 40 years, M-14 for 41 to 45 years, and M-13 for 46 to 50 years, then reduced by two units for every five years, that is, M-11 for 51 to 55 years, M-9 for 56 to 60 years, M-7 for 61 to 65 years and M-5 for 66 to 70 years."

13.In view of ratio of the above judgment, the net income of the deceased is to be counted after deduction of tax and future benefit have to be given @ 25% in case of self employed above the age of 40 years.
Apparently the salary of the deceased is not taxable.
Similarly, since the deceased was a self employed, 25% of enhancement of salary be also given to the petitioners.

In the case in hand, the deceased was having 4 dependents apart from him before accident and he was presumed to be spending 1/4th of his income on his personal expenses i.e. Rs. 3000/- (1/4 th of Rs. 12000/-).

Accordingly, the income for the purpose of loss of Neelam Vs. Pramod Kumar Yadav &

14.

To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased, as per the judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Sarla Verma vs Delhi Transport Corporation, 2009 ACJ 1298.

sentences.text: Since deceased, being 40 years plus of age, at the time of accident, a multiplier of 14 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.

Accordingly, this amount of Rs.18,90,000/- is allowed to petitioners towards loss of dependency.
15.As per judgment in the case of Shree Ram General Ins. Co. Ltd. Vs. Bhagat Singh Rawat & Ors.

Civil Appeal Nos. 2410-241 2/2023 decided by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India on 27.03.2023
Accordingly, this amount of Rs. 11,84,400/- is awarded to the petitioner towards loss Neelam Vs. Pramod Kumar Yadav & ors.
 of dependency.
The question with regard to contributory negligence has already been decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, as discussed above.
Accordingly, a fresh award to the tune of 60% of the total amount i.e. Rs. 26,47,000/- which includes 164 months and 19 days interest @ 9% per annum i.e. Rs. 14,62,437.9,8 from the date of fling of report under section 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act i.e. 27.04.2010 till passing this award is passed in favour of petitioners and against the respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co., details of which are well mentioned in the attached proforma.
17.There
is no dispute with regard to the bifurcation of the award amount, as made in impugned award dated 10.10.2017.
Accordingly, the terms of disbursement of compensation amount would remain same in terms of the impugned award dated 10.10.2017.
18.Accordingly
, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. is directed to deposit the above said awarded amount as compensation in this case, within the jurisdiction of this Tribunal at SBI, Rohini Court Branch,
Delhi within 30 days from today under intimation of deposition of the awarded amount to be given by respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. to the petitioners and their advocate failing which the respondent no.
3 / Ins. Co. shall be liable to pay further interest @ 9% per annum on the amount of Rs. 11,84,400/-
from the date of award till its realization.
Neelam Vs. Pramod Kumar Yadav & ors.

19.Interim amount, if any paid to the petitioners be deducted from this amount.
